jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About us

Forus is building an AI-powered network that connects doctors, pharmacies, payers, and biopharma to accelerate new science to patients.

Our platform automates the complexity between a doctor prescribing a medicine and a patient starting treatment, including insurance coverage, financial assistance, and supply chain navigation. We provide this support free to doctors and patients, helping them get life-changing medicine faster, cheaper, and easier. The resulting network enables biopharma companies to design better research, launch new drugs more effectively, and invest in harder-to-treat conditions.

Forus has exceptional product-market fit and is growing rapidly through organic adoption:

  • Accelerating scale: We already support patients across more than 85% of ZIP codes and partner with 9 of top 15 largest biopharma companies in the world.

  • AI-native, durable model: Our business becomes stronger as AI improves, as every new doctor, patient, and partner makes the network more valuable.

  • Backing to build for the long term: We raised $300M+ from leading investors to build an exceptional team and unlock the full scale of the opportunity.

Our number one priority is scaling to market demand. We are looking for individuals who are high horsepower, high throughput, and hyper resourceful to help us increase capacity and grow. We move fast and need to move faster.

If we succeed, science will be the only limit to medicine.

All full-time roles are in person in New York.

About the role

As a Software Engineer on our team, you will work across the stack to solve business problems with software and build the foundation of our platform. The role requires that you develop a deep understanding of our product surface area and what drives our business, such that you can operate and drive impact both cross-functionally and independently. You will have end-to-end responsibility for projects, including definition, design, development, launch, and success––this includes ensuring your output has the expected impact on user growth, operational efficiency, or revenue generation.

This is a demanding role, with a high level of autonomy and responsibility. You will be expected to "act like an owner" and commit yourself to Forus' success. If you are low-ego, hungry to learn, and excited about intense, impactful work that drives both company growth and accelerated career progression, we want to hear from you.

If you join, you will:

  • Own large parts of our product surface area and drive the relevant roadmaps to deliver on specific outcomes (See below for focus areas)

  • Drive zero-to-one product development from conceptualization through production, collaborating with our go-to-market and operations teams

  • Build new features and products top-to-bottom: front-end, back-end, system design, debugging, and testing

  • Participate actively in client engagements, working directly with customers to understand requirements and deliver innovative solutions

  • Establish and improve engineering processes, tools, and systems that will allow us to scale the code base and team productivity over time

We need your help to:

  • Decipher and automate complex, branching workflows for insurance coverage, affordability programs, and fulfillment

    • Combining AI/ML approaches to achieve high precision document classification, unstructured data extraction, and reference-based question answering

    • Automating multi-step, path-dependent processes, using a combination of RPA/scraping approaches to navigate and operate third-party platforms

    • Building a state machine that drives system decisions and handles failure modes across a set of processes that are technically independent but practically intertwined

  • Scale across a growing range of drug classes, patient populations, and provider markets

    • Making our data and ML pipelines robust to variation and inconsistency in input data formats (e.g., clinical documentation structure and style)

    • Leveraging empirical data to build and continuously update our understanding of opaque external systems (e.g., insurance company policies)

    • Creating consumer-grade experiences for patients, physicians, and other users that incorporate intuitive AI-powered workflows

  • Use our network to help biopharma partners accelerate drug development, launch, and access

    • Translating large volumes of heterogeneous data into reliable insights, informing decisions like clinical indication selection, launch markets, and insurer negotiations

    • Developing predictive and simulation models to forecast outcomes such as clinical trial site performance, drug adoption rates, and the impact of rebates/subsidies

    • Using real-time data and direct engagement channels to enroll criteria-matching patients and physicians in clinical studies and access programs

We’re looking for you if you have:

  • Strong programming skills and general Computer Science knowledge

  • Relevant engineering experience at fast-growing product-driven companies

  • Proficiency across a range of full-stack web development technologies (we use Python, React, Typescript, PostgreSQL, and Kubernetes)

  • Strong written and verbal communication that allows you to be an effective participant in both internal debates and external relationships

  • Track record of moving quickly, finding shortcuts, and going to unreasonable lengths to deliver on goals

  • High NPS with your former teammates

This is a list of ideal qualifications for this position. If you don't meet every single one of them, you should still consider applying! We’re excited to work with people from underrepresented backgrounds, and we encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.

Working with us

Forus is based in New York, with our full team working out of a beautiful and spacious office in SoHo. 

We run as a high-trust environment with high autonomy, which requires that everyone is fully competent and operates in line with our principles:

  • Do the math. Be rigorous, assume nothing. Break problems down and reason from the ground up. Stay open to changing your mind.

  • Resourceful optimism. Assume problems are solvable. Be audacious. Resist false constraints and push beyond the obvious before deciding.

  • Spit it out. Speak directly, invite critique, avoid equivocation. We want right answers, not comfortable ones. All killer, no filler.

  • Raise the bar. Hold a high standard for your pace and execution, and elevate the performance of the team around you. Mamba mentality.

  • Fight for users. Start with users’ realities, not ours. Resist optimizing for internal convenience over user outcomes.

We provide competitive compensation with meaningful equity (for full-time employees). Everyone who joins will be a major contributor to our success, and we reflect this through ownership and pay.

We also provide rich benefits to ensure you can focus on creating impact (for full-time employees):

  • Fully covered medical, vision, and dental insurance.

  • Memberships for One Medical, Talkspace, Teladoc, and Kindbody.

  • Unlimited paid time off (PTO) and 16 weeks of parental leave.

  • 401K plan setup, FSA option, commuter benefits, and DashPass.

  • Lunch at the office every day and Dinner at the office after 6:30 pm.


Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our company’s size and industry, and are one part of the total compensation package that also includes equity, benefits, and other opportunities at Forus (for full-time employees). Individual pay decisions are ultimately based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, geography, and balancing internal equity.

Forus is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law.

About the role

As a member of the Clinical Intelligence Review team at Generator Health, you will use your managed care expertise to optimize the quality, accuracy, and efficiency of our AI models and clinical workflows. You will own the review of all clinical artifacts our system produces – using cutting-edge AI tooling to build a view of accuracy that stitches together clinical context, payer requirements, and regulatory compliance. Using your clinical judgement and nuanced auditing, you will help build the clinical guidance our models and clinical teams use to continuously improve our system’s outputs.

This is a hands-on role centered on clinical review, structured feedback, and iterative improvement. You’ll look beyond individual cases to identify recurring problems, synthesize learnings into clinical guidance, and assess whether changes improve quality and throughput. We’re looking for someone who thrives in detailed clinical work and is excited to use AI to solve one of the most complex and time-consuming problems in healthcare operations.

This is a demanding role with a high level of autonomy and responsibility. You will be expected to act like an owner: prioritize effectively, surface problems early, and follow through until they’re resolved. If you are low-ego, hungry to learn, and motivated by consequential clinical work, we want to hear from you.

If you join, you will:

  • Audit a high volume of prior authorizations and AI-generated clinical outputs for accuracy, completeness, and alignment with the medical record and applicable payer criteria.

  • Apply evidence-based clinical reasoning to complex or ambiguous cases, distinguish clinically meaningful errors from minor issues, and help build a system that scales your expertise.

  • Identify recurring error patterns, gaps in clinical guidance, and edge cases; investigate their underlying causes and recommend improvements to review standards and workflows.

  • Apply AI tools to clinical review and auditing, critically evaluate their outputs, and identify ways to increase throughput while maintaining a high standard of clinical quality.

  • Own the quality and timeliness of your work, meet review expectations, and follow issues through to resolution.

     

We’re looking for you if you have:

  • A Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree and 2–10 years of professional experience, including hands-on managed care work in prior authorization, utilization management, appeals, or clinical quality at a health plan, pharmacy benefit manager (PBM), or similar organization.

  • Excellent clinical reasoning: you can synthesize medical records, medication histories, payer criteria, and clinical evidence, work through ambiguity, and clearly explain a defensible conclusion.

  • Strong systems thinking: you look beyond individual errors to recognize recurring patterns, identify root causes, and improve how similar cases are reviewed.

  • Precise written communication and attention to detail, with the ability to provide structured feedback that makes the issue, its clinical significance, and the needed correction clear.

  • High ownership and strong execution: you work independently, prioritize effectively, and reliably deliver accurate work at high volume.

  • Excitement about working with and applying AI to clinical work, paired with intellectual curiosity, a willingness to experiment, and the judgement to challenge AI outputs and revise your own conclusions when the evidence warrants it.

This is a list of ideal qualifications for this position. If you don't meet every single one of them, you should still consider applying! We’re excited to work with people from underrepresented backgrounds, and we encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.

Forus is based in New York, with our full team working out of a beautiful and spacious office in SoHo. 

We run as a high-trust environment with high autonomy, which requires that everyone is fully competent and operates in line with our principles:

  • Do the math. Be rigorous, assume nothing. Break problems down and reason from the ground up. Stay open to changing your mind.

  • Resourceful optimism. Assume problems are solvable. Be audacious. Resist false constraints and push beyond the obvious before deciding.

  • Spit it out. Speak directly, invite critique, avoid equivocation. We want right answers, not comfortable ones. All killer, no filler.

  • Raise the bar. Hold a high standard for your pace and execution, and elevate the performance of the team around you. Mamba mentality.

  • Fight for users. Start with users’ realities, not ours. Resist optimizing for internal convenience over user outcomes.

We provide competitive compensation with meaningful equity (for full-time employees). Everyone who joins will be a major contributor to our success, and we reflect this through ownership and pay.

We also provide rich benefits to ensure you can focus on creating impact (for full-time employees):

  • Fully covered medical, vision, and dental insurance.

  • Memberships for One Medical, Talkspace, Teladoc, and Kindbody.

  • Unlimited paid time off (PTO) and 16 weeks of parental leave.

  • 401K plan setup, FSA option, commuter benefits, and DashPass.

  • Lunch at the office every day and Dinner at the office after 6:30 pm.


Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our company’s size and industry, and are one part of the total compensation package that also includes equity, benefits, and other opportunities at Forus (for full-time employees). Individual pay decisions are ultimately based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, geography, and balancing internal equity.

Forus is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law.

Our platform automates the complexity between a doctor prescribing a medicine and a patient starting treatment, including insurance coverage, financial assistance, and supply chain navigation. We provide this support free to doctors and patients, helping them get life-changing medicine faster, cheaper, and easier. The resulting network enables biopharma companies to design better research, launch new drugs more effectively, and invest in harder-to-treat conditions.

Forus has exceptional product-market fit and is growing rapidly through organic adoption:

 - Accelerating scale: We already support patients across more than 85% of ZIP codes and partner with 9 of top 15 largest biopharma companies in the world.

 - AI-native, durable model: Our business becomes stronger as AI improves, as every new doctor, patient, and partner makes the network more valuable.

 - Backing to build for the long term: We raised $300M+ from leading investors to build an exceptional team and unlock the full scale of the opportunity.

Our number one priority is scaling to market demand. We are looking for individuals who are high horsepower, high throughput, and hyper resourceful to help us increase capacity and grow. We move fast and need to move faster.

If we succeed, science will be the only limit to medicine.

All full-time roles are in person in New York.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As part of our Strategic Finance team, you will help drive how the company plans, allocates resources, and makes decisions as we scale. You will work directly with the CEO and leadership team to translate strategy into financial models, evaluate key bets, and ensure we are investing behind the highest-impact opportunities. 

This role sits at the center of the business, spanning growth, product, operations, and fundraising. You will build the models and frameworks that define how we think about market expansion, unit economics, and long-term strategy, while also helping us operate with rigor day-to-day.

This is a demanding role, with a high level of autonomy and responsibility. You will be expected to "act like an owner" and commit yourself to Forus' success. If you are low-ego, hungry to learn, and excited about intense, impactful work that drives both company growth and accelerated career progression, we want to hear from you.




IF YOU JOIN, YOU WILL:

 - Build and own financial models that shape how Forus plans, forecasts, and makes high-stakes decisions

 - Partner with product, growth, and operations teams to define unit economics and evaluate where we should invest to drive the most impact

 - Analyze performance across the business, identifying what’s working, what’s not, and where we should double down or change course

 - Lead scenario modeling and sensitivity analyses to support decisions around pricing, market expansion, hiring, and capital allocation

 - Work directly with the CEO and leadership team on key initiatives, including new business lines, strategic partnerships, and fundraising strategy

 - Help design and evolve how the company operates, including planning cadence, resource allocation, and financial discipline as we scale

 - 2–10 years of experience in strategic finance, investment banking, private equity, growth equity, or a similar high-rigor analytical role

 - Ability to go from an ambiguous question to a structured answer with minimal guidance

  • Scope and spearhead AI augmentation and automation projects across our product surface area, including: Unintuitive classifications, Data extraction and summarization, Precise content generation, Reference-based search and question answering, Process outcome prediction, Probabilistic triggering of workflows, and Multimodal LLM-powered bots

  • Stay on top of emerging AI methods and guide decisions around which models and techniques to adopt––including evaluating when to use open-source models, proprietary models, and custom fine-tuning approaches

  • Establish research strategies for various AI methods, including rigorous experimentation and evaluation protocols that account for accuracy, consistency, interpretability, and real-world impact

  • Develop novel algorithms and techniques to address core research problems in natural language processing, data extraction, and autonomous reasoning (e.g., few-shot learning, agentic reasoning, and multi-modal interaction)

    • Combining AI/ML approaches to achieve high precision document classification, unstructured data extraction, and reference-based question answering

    • Automating multi-step, path-dependent processes, using a combination of RPA/scraping approaches to navigate and operate third-party platforms

    • Building a state machine that drives system decisions and handles failure modes across a set of processes that are technically independent but practically intertwined

  • Scale across a growing range of drug classes, patient populations, and provider markets

    • Making our data and ML pipelines robust to variation and inconsistency in input data formats (e.g., clinical documentation structure and style)

    • Leveraging empirical data to build and continuously update our understanding of opaque external systems (e.g., insurance company policies)

    • Creating consumer-grade experiences for patients, physicians, and other users that incorporate intuitive AI-powered workflows

  • Use our network to help biopharma partners accelerate drug development, launch, and access

    • Translating large volumes of heterogeneous data into reliable insights, informing decisions like clinical indication selection, launch markets, and insurer negotiations

    • Developing predictive and simulation models to forecast outcomes such as clinical trial site performance, drug adoption rates, and the impact of rebates/subsidies

    • Using real-time data and direct engagement channels to enroll criteria-matching patients and physicians in clinical studies and access programs

  • Strong programming skills and general Computer Science knowledge

  • Research background in ML/NLP, demonstrated through publications in top-tier conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP) or significant open-source contributions

  • Experience working on complex ML problems (e.g., data-efficient learning, reasoning agents, or multi-step workflows) and deploying those solutions in production environments

  • Deep understanding of modern ML methods, including transformer architectures, attention mechanisms, reinforcement learning, and multimodal models — with proficiency in deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX

  • Strong written and verbal communication that allows you to be an effective participant in both internal debates and external relationships

  • Track record of moving quickly, finding shortcuts, and going to unreasonable lengths to deliver on goals

  • High NPS with your former teammates

You will turn product improvements into coordinated launch moments, clear education, and measurable proof of impact that drive deeper adoption, stronger relationships, and greater advocacy across both individual practices and enterprise provider organizations.

You will work across Product, Customer Success, and other functions to shape positioning, prepare customer-facing teams, communicate our roadmap, and ensure every launch continues producing value after release. Success means providers see Forus as an increasingly important part of how their organization operates and feel that the product is getting materially better every month.

 - Create practice- and organization-level communications that demonstrate how Forus is reducing work, improving medication access, and supporting better patient outcomes

  • Secure our corporate and identity surface, including SSO, device and endpoint security, SaaS hardening, and access across the employee lifecycle

  • Design isolation and data-flow controls for agentic AI systems, defending against sensitive-data leakage across model pipelines and tool use

  • Build the automation and security-as-code that lets engineers move quickly while implementing the technical controls behind SOC 2, HIPAA, and HITRUST.

  • Partner with Legal, Compliance, and GTM to translate regulatory and customer requirements into practical controls that we can ship

We'll be most excited if you have:

  • 7+ years in security engineering, grounded in a strong software engineering foundation. You design and implement systems, not just review them

  • Deep, hands-on cloud security experience across AWS and/or GCP, including infrastructure as code and building security foundations rather than only configuring managed services

  • Range across infrastructure, application, identity, and detection and response, with the judgment to operate as the first security engineer

  • Experience protecting sensitive data at scale; experience with PHI, HIPAA, or similarly regulated data is a strong plus

  • Comfort designing security controls for LLMs, AI agents, and the data flows around them

The engineering problems at Forus span user-facing product, complex backend systems, AI and agents, data, and enterprise deployment. Our software has to absorb enormous variation across providers, medicines, payers, pharmacies, clinical systems, and enterprise environments; reason over messy information; interact with systems we do not control; and reliably execute real-world workflows where the happy path is rarely the only path.

  • Provider Product & Growth - Build the core product providers and their staff use every day and drive its adoption, activation, engagement, expansion, and organic growth. The challenge is making an extremely complicated underlying system feel simple while supporting everyone from independent practices to some of the largest provider organizations in the country

  • Core Platform & Automation - Build the backend systems that power Forus and execute the work behind every prescription, spanning workflow and state systems, integrations, data and document infrastructure, operational tooling, and AI- and agent-powered subsystems.   • Life Sciences Engineering - Build products with leading biopharma companies to help innovative medicines reach more patients. We have more customer demand and product opportunities than we can pursue, so the work starts with deciding where technology can create the most value and build the biggest businesses, then building with customers and turning the best ideas into products that scale across medicines and companies. Over time, we are working toward becoming a critical technology and execution layer across the full lifecycle of medicine

This is a demanding role, with a high level of autonomy and responsibility. You will be expected to "act like an owner" and commit yourself to Forus' success. If you are low-ego, hungry to learn, and excited about intense, impactful work that drives both company growth and accelerated career progression, we want to hear from you.

  • Stay hands-on, writing and reviewing production code, leading architecture decisions, and taking on hard or ambiguous problems yourself when that is the fastest path forward

  • Work directly with providers, life sciences partners, and our operations team; You will be expected to fully understand and internalize the needs of your users and build for them

  • Raise the ceiling on how your team builds with AI, and push the team to always be experimenting with more productive ways to develop software

  • 6+ years building software, with a track record of shipping products that real users depend on

  • 2+ years leading engineers, with clear accountability for both team output and the growth and performance of the people on it

  • Full-stack range. You have built and operated the backend systems and the interfaces on top of them, and you can make credible calls across the whole stack

  • A real hiring track record. You have recruited strong engineers who joined in part because you were the one selling the role

  • The ability to go from an ambiguous business problem to a clear, structured, shipped solution

  • A track record of moving quickly, finding shortcuts, and going to unreasonable lengths to deliver on goals

  • High NPS with your former teammates and reports

  • Spit it out. Speak directly, invite critique, avoid equivocation. We want right answers, not comfortable ones. All killer, no filler.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As InfoSec Manager at Forus, you will own the infrastructure, security posture, and systems that enable our team and protect the organization. This is a hands-on infrastructure role: you will implement systems, troubleshoot issues, make architecture calls on tooling and access, and take on hard operational problems yourself. You will also own the strategic side - building security programs, managing vendor relationships, and ensuring that as Forus scales, our infrastructure and compliance architecture scales with us.

InfoSec at Forus sits at the intersection of product engineering, operations, and security. You need to enable a fast-moving team to ship quickly, work seamlessly with external vendors and contractors, navigate compliance and regulatory requirements, and build visibility into what software and systems the organization is actually using. The work spans hands-on troubleshooting, project execution (migrations, system implementations), ongoing security and compliance programs, and vendor management.

This is a demanding role, with a high level of autonomy and responsibility. You will be expected to "act like an owner" and commit yourself to Forus' success. If you are low-ego, hungry to learn, and excited about intense, impactful work that drives both company growth and accelerated career progression, we want to hear from you.

 - Own Forus' InfoSec infrastructure end to end - from access controls and identity management through device management, cloud systems, compliance, and security posture

 - Implement and manage core IT systems (identity and access, SIEMs, shadow IT visibility) and make credible calls on which new tools and systems the organization should adopt

 - Manage relationships with external IT vendors, from contracting and feedback loops through escalations, approvals, and accountability

 - Build and execute Forus' security program - identifying gaps in our posture, introducing new tools and configurations, and regulating permissions and access as we scale

 - Lead and automate onboarding and offboarding workflows to ensure seamless employee experience and tight security as the team grows

 - Work cross-functionally with engineering, operations, legal, and compliance to translate business and regulatory needs into technical architecture and operational practices

 - 5+ years in IT operations, infrastructure, or security roles with a track record of building systems and scaling organizations

 - Hands-on experience in a startup or high-growth environment where you've worn multiple hats and built IT practices from the ground up, not just maintained them

 - Demonstrated ability to work seamlessly cross-functionally with people, engineering, operations, legal, and compliance - you understand what each team needs and you translate between them fluently

 - Experience managing employees at scale, including facilitating smooth on/offboarding workflows and thinking systematically about identity and access as the team grows

 - High agency and ownership mentality; you see problems and solve them rather than escalate, and you drive outcomes even when they span multiple teams or vendors

 - Strong written and verbal communication that allows you to be an effective participant in both internal debates and external vendor relationships

 - Track record of moving quickly, finding shortcuts, and going to unreasonable lengths to deliver on goals

 - Resourceful optimism.  Assume problems are solvable. Be audacious. Resist false constraints and push beyond the obvious before deciding.

 - Spit it out.  Speak directly, invite critique, avoid equivocation. We want right answers, not comfortable ones. All killer, no filler.

 - Raise the bar.  Hold a high standard for your pace and execution, and elevate the performance of the team around you. Mamba mentality.

 - Fight for users.  Start with users’ realities, not ours. Resist optimizing for internal convenience over user outcomes.
   

We provide competitive compensation with meaningful equity (for full-time employees). Everyone who joins will be a major contributor to our success, and we reflect this through ownership and pay.

  • Lead providers through workflow change by mapping stakeholders, building champions, securing executive buy-in, and expanding successful usage across teams and workflows

  • Build trusted relationships with provider teams at every level, from frontline staff to executive leadership, creating users who advocate for Forus internally and externally

  • Analyze account health, adoption patterns, provider behavior, and operational friction to identify risks early, uncover expansion opportunities, and drive action

  • Lead business reviews, adoption reviews, and strategic planning conversations that connect provider priorities to measurable outcomes and continued platform expansion

  • Own provider escalations end-to-end, coordinating across Operations and Product, keeping customers informed and internal owners accountable through resolution

  • Define and refine the Provider Success playbook, including onboarding plans, adoption frameworks, lifecycle stages, health metrics, escalation paths, and stakeholder-engagement models

We’re looking for you if you have:

  • 2–10 years of experience in customer success, implementation, account management, client service, post-sales operations, or another customer-facing role, with a track record of owning customers through onboarding, adoption, expansion, retention, and escalation

  • A consultative approach to customer relationships: you can understand how an organization works, identify what matters, and guide stakeholders toward measurable outcomes

  • Strong operational and analytical judgment: you can manage a portfolio rigorously, use data to diagnose friction, and distinguish isolated requests from patterns that require action

  • Strong written and verbal communication that allows you to build trust with providers, align internal teams, and drive follow-through

  • Track record of moving quickly, finding shortcuts, and going to unreasonable lengths to deliver on goals
